tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash beat flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, released amid an intensifying China AI price war, before going fully open-source. A week of price-hike warnings led into V4 Pro's confirmed Aug 13 launch at sharply higher prices alongside Harness, DeepSeek's open-source answer to Claude Code.
whats_new: DeepSeek shipped a second multimodal model on Aug 24, per a single outlet with no model name or benchmark yet — still unclear whether it's distinct from the Aug 21 V4-Flash-Vision-Exp release, or delayed coverage of the same one.
why_it_matters: Treat the Aug 24 release as unconfirmed until a second source names the model or publishes a benchmark. For cost planning, the operative signal is still Aug 23's partial pricing rollback: the weekend surcharge is gone, but the underlying V4 Pro hike stands.

status.state: Weekend peak-pricing surcharge dropped, but the underlying V4 Pro hike still stands
status.detail: Harness exited preview at MIT-licensed v0.1 Aug 17, added multimodal/subagent support Aug 20, then folded Claude Code and Codex in as sub-agents Aug 21 — the same day V4-Flash-Vision-Exp shipped. DeepSeek ended the weekend peak-pricing surcharge Aug 23, even as cumulative prices remain up 355% since the hike. A single outlet reported a second multimodal model Aug 24, unconfirmed.

beats.headline: An unshipped agent-tool preview and a mixed hands-on verdict, before the price war heats up
beats.summary: Memeburn previews 'DeepSeek Code' as a confirmed-but-unshipped project on Aug 5, foreshadowing the Harness tool that ships Aug 13. Five days later, The New Stack's hands-on test finds V4-Flash's 'better and cheaper than V4-Pro' promise holds only partly.

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for over a week before DeepSeek confirms anything
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Investing.com, TechNode, The Next Web, China Daily, Semafor, Mashable, a CITIC Securities note, and regional coverage all flag a coming DeepSeek price increase for a week and a half before the official V4 Pro launch makes it real; the-decoder.com's Aug 12 comparison still finds DeepSeek beating Microsoft's MAI Code on price and performance as the hike looms.

beats.headline: DeepSeek publicizes a dedicated team building agent tools to rival Claude Code
beats.summary: A Pi-founder claim that DeepSeek plus Pi already beats Claude Code opens the day; hours later Bloomberg is first to report DeepSeek forming a team aimed squarely at Anthropic's Claude Code, corroborated same-day by PYMNTS' "new team" framing and repeated by briefs.co and TradingView into Aug 13 — hours before that team's tool ships.

beats.headline: Off-topic Claude Code posts, an unrelated harness tool, and a wave of Qwen 3.8 coverage ride the same keyword clusters
beats.summary: Not part of the DeepSeek story: two Anthropic Claude Code/Cowork posts, an unrelated Hacker News 'harness' project (Archon), and ten Qwen 3.8 pieces (release, hardware runs, comparisons vs Kimi/GPT-5.6/Opus) — swept in by shared 'Claude Code'/'harness'/'open weight' keywords. Flagged for transparency, not narrative continuity.

beats.headline: A quiet OpenRouter build becomes DeepSeek's officially confirmed V4 Pro release, at sharply higher prices
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only with no announcement page; a day later, Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times confirm it as a deliberate release at sharply higher user prices, with The Information framing it as a direct challenge to Kimi K3.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, a free Claude Code rival, then exits preview at MIT-licensed v0.1
beats.summary: VentureBeat, The New Stack, 36Kr, and TechNode report the free, open-sourced Harness tool shipping alongside pricier V4-Pro, and it lands on China's state supercomputing network. Four days later, GuruFocus and MarkTechPost confirm the MIT-licensed v0.1 developer preview, followed by Pandaily's report of Harness's first post-beta update: 14 changes adding multimodal and subagent support.

beats.headline: Recap widens to a US-China AI-race frame, quantifies the hike, then pits V4 Pro's price and capability against Qwen 3.8 Max
beats.summary: Coverage widens: benchmark gains cited, the hike framed as a strategy shift and a US-China race, Forbes quantifies it at 14x the cheapest model, and TheSequence reviews it alongside GLM-5.3 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Willison's Artificial Analysis check puts Qwen 3.8 27B one point behind V4 Pro — DeepSeek's open-weight edge is thin. Memeburn reframes the hike against Qwen 3.8 Max.

beats.headline: Harness folds Claude Code and Codex in as sub-agents the same day DeepSeek ships a multimodal model pitched against Opus 4.8
beats.summary: 36Kr reports Harness folding Claude Code and Codex in as callable sub-agents, alongside a same-day walkthrough. Hours later, eight outlets corroborate V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, DeepSeek's first head-to-head multimodal comparison against Opus 4.8 rather than Claude Code.

beats.headline: DeepSeek drops its weekend peak-pricing surcharge, even as cumulative peak prices remain up sharply
beats.summary: Bloomberg and a second outlet report DeepSeek ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge for API users the same day a comparison piece puts cumulative peak-price increases at 355% since the original hike — an incremental de-escalation, not a reversal of the underlying V4 Pro price increase.

beats.headline: DeepSeek ships a second multimodal model Aug 24 — single-source, no name or benchmark yet
beats.summary: TahawulTech.com is the only outlet reporting it so far. It's unclear whether this is a genuinely new release or delayed coverage of the Aug 21 V4-Flash-Vision-Exp launch.

open_questions: Is the Aug 24 "new multimodal model" a distinct release from V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, or delayed/duplicate coverage of the same Aug 21 launch — what's the model's actual name and spec?
Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
Forbes prices V4 Pro at 14x DeepSeek's cheapest model — is that still cheaper than Qwen 3.8 Max per token, or has DeepSeek lost its price edge to Alibaba?

Now that Harness folds in Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents, has it pivoted from a Claude Code rival to an orchestration layer — and does that require API access to those tools rather than being a drop-in replacement?
Does V4-Flash-Vision-Exp's "comes close to Opus 4.8" claim rest on a published benchmark, or is it qualitative positioning?
Does ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge signal a broader course-correction on pricing, or is it a narrow carve-out that leaves the underlying V4 Pro hike intact?
take_for_builders: Hold off updating any DeepSeek multimodal comparison until a second outlet confirms the Aug 24 model's name and benchmarks; separately, re-check current weekend/off-peak API rates before locking a cost model — pricing has now moved twice since the August hike.
